name: Compact the non-Marlin CUDA Graph tail
hypothesis: Only dependency-legal producer-consumer boundaries that remove a materialization or graph node can reduce the remaining tail; scheduler-only tuning is already below the observed opportunity scale.
derivation: Non-Marlin kernels total 1.372 ms per output decision. The 0.180 ms ceiling keeps recurrent, attention and normalization mathematical work mandatory and exposes only a bounded launch/materialization fraction.

evidence.claim: Complete node-expanded non-Marlin residual rather than a KERNEL-only graph summary.
